subject: Request: Availability tolerance & latency exception for Holbrook Health order form
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@holbrookhealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: availability tolerance & latency exception

Hi Nikhil,

Quick note from Holbrook Security/IT: our procurement team is finalizing the order form and Legal is asking for a formal exception to the standard availability SLA for a pilot deployment in our East Coast region. We're requesting: 
- Availability tolerance: 99.5% monthly (instead of standard 99.9%) for the first 6 months
- Latency: p95 250ms for inference on short prompts; if p95 exceeds 250ms for >48h we want an automatic rollback to a lower-latency model variant

Attached is a short PDF with our ask and the proposed routing constraints. Can Redwood provide:
1) a clean addendum (SLA exhibit) we can attach to the Order Form
2) suggested order-form language for committed throughput and the exception term length
3) a list of evidence you can provide (uptime reports, latency histograms, regional routing terms)

We need to share a draft with Legal by Tuesday EOD PT.

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Platform Ops
Holbrook Health
[Attachment: Holbrook-SLA-exception-request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver@holbrookhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability tolerance & latency exception

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Looping in Marissa (Account Lead) and Karthik (Service Guarantees) to scope the addendum and order-form language. We can draft an Availability Annex that captures the temporary tolerance and the rollback/variant fallback behavior you describe.

Quick clarifying Qs so we draft precisely for Legal:
- Pilot scope: how many unique users / concurrent qps should we size for the committed throughput?
- Is the 6-month term fixed or do you want milestone-based re-evaluation after month 3?
- Any regional data-residency constraints beyond routing to east/us-east?

We will share an initial annex + marked-up order form by EOD Tuesday.

Nikhil
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Redwood logo]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver@holbrookhealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability tolerance & latency exception

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the concrete targets. Attached are two files: a proposed Availability Annex you can attach to your MSA/SOW and a redlined Order Form snippet that contains the exception term and committed throughput placeholders. Key callouts in the Annex: 
- Temporary availability tolerance: 99.5% monthly for a 6-month pilot, automatically reverting to standard 99.9% after month 6 unless both parties agree in writing.
- Latency safeguard: Redwood will monitor p95; if p95 > 250ms for a continuous 48-hour window we will failover traffic to a pre-agreed lower-latency model variant and notify Holbrook within 30 minutes. Failover is reversible after latency normalizes for 72 hours.
- Evidence and reporting: weekly uptime and latency histograms; one-time access to a 30-day historical report on request; annual SOC2 excerpts available upon procurement NDA.

I've left the committed throughput and pricing placeholders in the Order Form so Procurement can fill numbers. Karthik — flagged you for the evidence and rollback mechanics; please add any operational constraints.

Attachments: Redwood-Proposed-Availability-Annex.docx (docx), OrderForm_HLBK-038.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver@holbrookhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability tolerance & latency exception

Marissa / Nikhil —

Reviewed the Annex. A few technical clarifications / suggestions for Legal & Procurement to consider before we finalize:
1) Measurement windows: we recommend p95 measured across 5-minute rolling windows aggregated hourly (this avoids transient spikes triggering failover). Will call that out in section 2.1.
2) Failover mechanics: we need a pre-approved lower-latency model variant (we've noted an internal model tag: redwood-gold-8q) and a traffic-shift plan (gradual 10% increments every 5 minutes up to 100% unless manual abort). We'll include the operational playbook as an appendix, but for the Annex we can reference the playbook and state that Redwood will provide a time-stamped incident report within 4 hours of failover initiation.
3) Evidence: for procurement sign-off we can provide weekly CSV exports of uptime metrics and a one-time extract of request-level latency distributions (PII redacted). For audit requests, SOC2 attestations require a separate add-on; we've noted that in the Annex.

Also recommend the Order Form includes a short clause: "Pilot exception limited to OrderForm HLBK-038 and applies only to services deployed in the specified region(s) for the stated pilot period."

I'll drop a clean PDF of the Annex with these edits by EOD today.

-Karthik
Director, Service Guarantees | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-Availability-Annex-v2.pdf (pdf)]

Marissa / Nikhil / Karthik —

This looks good and thanks to the team for the quick turnaround. A couple of small asks from Legal:
- Replace the automatic reversion language with: "Reversion to standard SLA at month 6 unless Holbrook requests extension in writing and Redwood agrees." (legal prefers Holbrook-driven extension rather than automatic).
- Add a single sentence to evidence section: "Redwood will provide a signed, time-stamped uptime summary for each month of the pilot upon request."

If you can produce a final Annex PDF with those two edits and a DocuSign-ready Order Form by tomorrow morning (Friday), we can execute procurement and route to Legal.

Also, we'll confirm committed throughput (expected peak 1200 qps, sustained 400 qps) and include that in the OrderForm_HLBK-038.xlsx.

If you want to call to confirm language I can do 10:30 PT tomorrow. Otherwise please send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
